target.statement: X-Coder-Qwen2.5-14B-RL attains 67.5 avg@8 on LiveCodeBench v5 (SFT-then-RL on fully synthetic tasks/solutions/tests).
target.table_ref: Table 1 (SFT-then-RL Approaches, Stage 2), row 'X-Coder-Qwen2.5-14B-RL', column 'LCB v5'
target.dataset: LiveCodeBench v5 (268 problems; evaluation pass-rate over 8 samples)

compute.basis: The cell requires a full two-stage post-training run: SFT of a 14B model for 8 epochs on ~200k long-CoT synthetic samples (~1e21 FLOPs) followed by 40k-example GRPO with executable-reward sandboxing, i.e. multi-GPU-node training; on an 8-core CPU laptop this is effectively infeasible (the 200000-min figure is a token-flop lower bound, not a realistic completion time).

blockers: Requires training 7B/14B LLMs: 200k-prompt long-CoT SFT for 8 epochs plus 40k GRPO RL (multi-GPU cluster of A100/H100-class GPUs, ~80 GB VRAM per GPU with sharding)

The data-construction pipeline that produced the training artifacts depends on closed/proprietary models (GPT-4o-0513 for feature extraction, GPT-o3-mini for task formulation, GPT-5-High as solvability proxy) and very large open teachers (DeepSeek-R1-0528 671B, Qwen3-235B-A22B) that cannot run on a laptop; released data mitigates but does not remove this
RL reward requires an isolated Redis-based execution sandbox running untrusted model-generated programs at high concurrency
Evaluation protocol itself (avg@8, 32k-token generations, 14B model) needs ~64 GB+ RAM/VRAM and hours of generation, far beyond a laptop
title: X-Coder: Advancing Competitive Programming with Synthetic Tasks, Solutions, and Tests
